# P212 exact eight-file reader and retained-output entry — source only

2026-09-11 UTC. AUTHOR_SOURCE_ONLY_PROPOSAL / HOLD_OPERATIONAL / HOLD_EXTERNAL.
This new preparation alone is owned. It is not B1-B4 closure, an S0 call,
an observation receipt, a materialization receipt or a fresh grant.

## Received premise and exactly changed source

Root's [full received source/policy decision](../p212_minimal_contract01_source_root01/RECEPTION.md)
is 10,139 bytes, SHA256
663fcfdaf3d0541acb3199f2bc31f0e55050f75b74480c025df97abbf78ac1f7,
with ten-payload seal
e2a1d505ebcaf7685a0e1f89cfe5f971514adb588265aefe0dab4bf3610a1c12.
It explicitly adopts the ordinary root key-tool/builtin bootstrap boundary.
No recursive key-reader/runtime observer is required or introduced here.
It still requires exact derivative/request review and a fresh observation grant.

file_keys.proposed.mjs.txt differs from the frozen 13,630-byte file_keys.mjs
only in its opening comment and the finite-file function's first
SOURCE_ENABLED false-to-true value. It is 13,660 bytes / 189 lines.
The guard check itself and every other body byte are preserved. The entire
directory-observation suffix, including its SOURCE_ENABLED=false guard,
is unchanged. capture.js, receive.mjs and every old template remain frozen
and disabled. This .txt derivative has no CLI or automatic invocation and
was not imported or executed. Its opened source guard is not authority.

FILE_REQUEST.proposed.json is the complete unchanged 1,979-byte old template,
not merely an equivalent parsed object. All eight entries retain exact order,
path, role, optionality, max_bytes, capture_hex=true and expected=null.
Its enabled flag remains false, permission_receipt and settlement_receipt null,
and source-gate status/purpose unchanged. Six 16 MiB candidates and two
optional 1 MiB configuration candidates total 102,760,448 bytes (98 MiB).
Optional is actual lexical ENOENT only; no absence, physical alias, file key,
installed version or observed closure is predicted.

The new exact entry clamps the activated request back to that entire
template after removing only the three allowed future activation fields.
The original reader then validates the full actual permission-reference
shape and every file entry before any candidate path operation. Other
purposes, new entries, expected-key filling, changed limits and follow-up
spellings are not this entry's scope even though the unmodified general
function body contains other separately gated roles.

## Complete new entry, canonical serializer and native capture

collect_files.proposed.mjs.txt is genuinely new, separately reviewable
304-line source, not inherited acceptance. It has three limited jobs:

1. Read the one fixed, later root-materialized request input, capped at
   65,536 bytes. A no-follow physical regular leaf, complete actual read-to-zero
   EOF, four ten-field endpoint/same-fd structures and successful close are
   required. Complete actual request bytes/hex and their pin are recorded
   OUTSIDE that request. Partial read/close errors remain explicitly partial.
   This root-owned request input is a request/provenance role, not a ninth
   host candidate or an observer of the key tool's own runtime.
2. Call only collectP212S0Files, once, with the exact eight-file request.
   No directory reader, help/version collector, old receiver, ELF decoder,
   alias follower, discovery routine, process enumerator or target executable
   is invoked. A returned FAILED_PARTIAL_PRESERVED object is kept in full,
   including every successful earlier row, partial last row and raw hex.
3. Serialize the complete returned value and request-input evidence to FD 1,
   preserving strings and exact integer fields. There is no JSON.stringify
   of one huge output object or single huge encoded output Buffer. No returned
   bytes are interpreted as ELF/configuration or executed. A normalized error
   is name/code/message data, not a claim to preserve an entire Error object.

The seven-line capture is the entire proposed native cmd. Under umask 077
and noclobber it exclusively opens the two exact future leaves, then maps
child FD 1 from parent 3 and FD 2 from parent 4, closes child 3/4, and execs
the trusted root Node key-tool entry without script arguments. It does not
mkdir, inspect a directory, load a physical capture script, use a pipeline,
background work, invoke env/kpsewhich, or launch a second operation.
The literal node command uses the ordinary trusted root shell PATH; no
resolved Node binary path, loader inventory or new runtime attestation is
claimed. This root key-tool launch is not either S0 help/version vector;
tool_vectors_invoked=false in its output refers to those measured S0 vectors.

A separately prepared fresh owned 0700 output directory is essential.
Its current existence, owner, contents, available capacity and keys are
unknown here. The entry requires distinct empty regular single-link FD 1/2;
fresh exclusive creation and ordinary ancestors/filesystem/parent remain
the adopted trust boundary, not protection against a hostile parent.
Stdin is inherited unused root-key-tool stdin; it is never opened or inspected.

## Canonical format and finite retention

The prospective stdout format is p212-ascii-canonical-json-v1: sorted own
enumerable object keys, original dense array order, null/boolean/safe integer
numbers (reject -0), and strings preserving every UTF-16 code unit.
Every code unit outside printable ASCII, and quote/backslash, is written
as lower-case backslash-u plus four hexadecimal digits. This includes each
surrogate unit; splitting the 16,384-unit chunks cannot replace or normalize
a Unicode value. Other printable ASCII, including every hex digit, is copied.
Exactly one final LF follows the complete JSON value. No getter/toJSON hook,
function, cyclic/nonplain object, unsupported numeric value or sparse array
is evaluated as data.

The writer has a 256 MiB / 268,435,456-byte stdout cap, 8 MiB entry-diagnostic
cap, 8,192 value-node bound and depth 32. One input-string chunk becomes at
most 98,304 encoded bytes. Each successful positive write return advances
the exact offset/count; zero/error/unsupported structure/bound failure is
failure, never success with a clipped suffix. FD 1's identity projection
and size are checked against actual reported writes, and a returned successful
FD 1 close is necessary for native zero. FD 2 stays available for a stdout
close failure and settles at ordinary actual native completion; no explicit
stderr-close, continuous snapshot or post-final-runtime attestation is claimed.

The eight-file reader retains at most 102,760,449 candidate bytes including
its one possible failing overflow sentinel, hence at most 205,520,898 hex
characters. These source-level bounds are not actual observations. The
256 MiB envelope cap leaves room above this candidate-hex bound and the small
bounded request/control structure; arbitrary unusual exception data can
still hit the fail-closed cap. The original reader still holds its own
buffers/hex strings in memory. Streaming the serializer adds no hard memory,
wall-time, storage reservation, filesystem-return or guaranteed-liveness claim.
The entry's diagnostic cap does not globally bound native bootstrap/runtime
stderr writes, which go to the separate raw file.

Normal reader partial/failure returns are serialized completely and produce
native 78, not acceptance. A request/entry exception or unreturned reader
produces native 79 and, when safe and no output progress is reported, a
failure envelope retaining the actual request-input and returned-value state.
Otherwise only best-effort diagnostic data is added to stderr while existing
partial stdout is preserved. Primary and secondary error descriptions are
kept when a failure-envelope write also fails. A fatal allocation/IO/process
failure can make the original internal reader rows or later transport
unavailable; reader_called=true/reader_returned=false does NOT prove no
candidate observation occurred. No missing internal value, byte suffix,
exception object or native return is reconstructed. No bytes/files are
overwritten, deleted, retried as observations, or reclassified as complete.

Native zero is only a candidate for later original-data reception. Require
the actual complete native request and every return/continuation, empty
separate native control output, the complete closed stdout file, empty raw
stderr, valid complete canonical value and every actual reader/input record.
Hash/count/preview/record status is not acceptance. Bootstrap/import/setup
failure can precede the entry; the raw redirections preserve diagnostics
once set up. An incomplete/truncated earlier native control return stays
incomplete and cannot be reconstructed from a later file.

## Source, input, authority and nonself receipt roles

ENTRY_REQUEST.proposed.json contains the complete exec_command arguments
and only an empty-input same-actual-session continuation proposal. Every
actual command/request/result/session/grant/materialization/target-directory/
input-key/canonical-acceptance field remains null or false. The proposed
cmd strings and source byte pins are DATA, never submitted operations.

|---|---|
| Exact sources/capture/request | Independent noncontributor reception, then root original reception of their complete current bytes. |
| Future physical source copies | Separate materialization scope and actual complete current copy keys/raw comparison; no launch from a source receipt. |
| Root-bound request | Only enabled/status/permission_receipt may change; exact complete bound bytes plus nonself external before/after keys, outside the request. The entry's read record is additional content evidence, not its own authority. |
| New one-observation authority | A fresh actual root grant, separately received and consumed before the exact native submission. A reference/path/hash or ROOT_BOUND label is not the grant. Both historical P212 grants stay consumed. |
| Actual returned data | Complete actual native originals, settled closed raw files and all complete/partial rows; then independent/root reception at the actual observed scope. |
| Installed interpretation/S0 | Separately source-gated DATA-only interpretation and bounded B1-B4 decisions; no automatic follow-up read, ELF execution, alias repair or tool call. |

This new envelope and up-to-256-MiB raw file are not compatible input to
the old S0 receive.mjs interface or its old 128-MiB per-file closed_raw
request/selected raw root. Neither is enabled. A future complete DATA-only
consumer must handle this exact format/size, preserve integer strings,
validate every actual hex byte and reconstruct/re-encode only for raw equality
checks against the actual entire file. No such interpretation/consumer source
is implemented or authorized here, and none may infer closure from eight
candidate names or reinterpret document checks as an observation canonical.
